title: Cache TTL proposed then revised after a stale-data concern
notes: Tests update/correction handling: an initial 1-hour TTL is proposed then revised down to 5 minutes after a stale-data concern is raised in the same session. Gold captures the final TTL plus the reasoning for the revision.

turns.text: For the product-price cache, let's set the TTL to 1 hour — prices don't change that often.
Setting the product-price cache TTL to 1 hour.

Actually, wait — marketing runs flash sales that change prices instantly and expect them live within a minute or two. A 1-hour TTL would show stale (pre-sale) prices for up to an hour during a flash sale launch. Let's drop it to 5 minutes instead.
Actually maybe even that's risky for flash sales — but 5 minutes is probably an acceptable tradeoff between staleness risk and cache hit rate, so let's go with that.

Understood — setting the TTL to 5 minutes instead of 1 hour. That caps worst-case price staleness during a flash sale to 5 minutes, which is an acceptable tradeoff against giving up some cache hit rate versus the 1-hour option.
Right, 5 minutes is the final number, not the original 1 hour — make sure that's clear in the config comments.
Confirmed: product-price cache TTL is 5 minutes. I'll add a config comment explaining the flash-sale staleness reasoning so nobody bumps it back to 1 hour without realizing why it's short.

gold_atoms.text: Set the product-price cache TTL to 5 minutes — NOT the initially proposed 1 hour.

A 1-hour product-price cache TTL would show stale pre-sale prices for up to an hour during a flash sale launch, since marketing expects flash-sale price changes to go live within a minute or two; 5 minutes caps worst-case staleness while still giving up some cache hit rate versus the 1-hour option.
